# Ademvnion

> Adem is building Vnion, wearable human enhancement. The software it ships
> today is free, runs in a browser, and needs no account: a robot design tool
> with real physics, and interactive teardowns of real open-source robots.

## Pages

- [Adem Forge](https://ademvnion.com/app/): free robot design software in the
  browser. Snap parts together, set mass, motor torque, joint limits and
  friction, press Run, and watch real physics (Google DeepMind's MuJoCo,
  compiled to WebAssembly) decide whether it works. Tasks report whether the
  robot lifted, travelled or stayed standing. Builds share as a link.
- [Inside the SO-ARM101](https://ademvnion.com/inside/so-arm101/): every part
  of a real open-source robot arm in 3D — six STS3215 servos, driver board,
  printed links — with what each part is, why it is there, what it costs, and
  what breaks without it. Parts can be hidden, the assembly exploded, the
  joints moved. Built from The Robot Studio's Apache-2.0 CAD and URDF.
- [Inside real robots](https://ademvnion.com/inside/): the teardown index.
- [Home](https://ademvnion.com/): what Adem and Vnion are.

## Notes

- Everything is free and needs no sign-up. There is no hardware for sale.
- Numbers on the teardown pages come from published CAD, datasheets and bills
  of materials, not estimates.
